sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Large-leaved lupine is a perennial native to western North America, usually 0.6–1.5 m tall. It grows in meadows, wetlands, streambanks and woodland edges; it is naturalised and sometimes invasive elsewhere.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and pods
sections.text: The palmate leaves usually have 9–17 leaflets. Pea-shaped flowers grow in upright racemes. The hairy pods dry and split open to release the seeds.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The seeds contain quinolizidine alkaloids and can poison livestock or wildlife when eaten in large amounts. Do not eat them.
